highlights: Surprise rate hike: the Central Bank raised the overnight policy rate 25bps to 9.00% and the banks' reserve ratio (SRR) 1 point to 3.00% from 9 Dec, as inflation rose to 8.3% in October. HNB Stockbrokers expects higher lending rates and slower credit growth, but only limited further mark-to-market losses on banks' government securities.

The market fell on 20 Nov: the ASPI closed at 21,369.72 (about −0.80% on the day) and the S&P SL20 at 6,075.28 (about −1.09%), on Rs 2.3bn turnover. Telecoms led the fall (SLT-Mobitel −3.10%, Dialog −2.04%), with banks, JKH and LIOC also lower. For the week the ASPI lost 2.97% (−654 points) and the S&P SL20 3.47%.

Foreigners were net buyers of Rs 0.88bn this week (bought Rs 1,227M, sold Rs 351.6M), almost all from Hosking Partners buying 5.18% of JAT Holdings (Rs 1.09bn of foreign buying in JAT). Dialog had the most foreign selling (about Rs 0.15bn).

Hosking Partners paid Rs 38.8 a share for its JAT Holdings (JAT.N0000) stake, well above this site's JAT fair value of Rs 21 (buy below Rs 17.80). Hosking says it will stay invested in Sri Lanka but commit much more only if the recovery proves lasting.
Global sell-off: on 19 Nov the Dow fell 2.19% and the S&P 500 2.02%, and on Friday morning Taiwan's TAIEX fell 6.16%, Korea's KOSPI 4.72% and Japan's Nikkei 4.49%.

keyPoints: CBSL raised the OPR 25bps to 9.00% and the SRR 1pp to 3.00%, as the long Middle East conflict kept energy and food prices high.
Inflation rose to 8.3% in October and is now expected to stay above the 5% target until the second half of 2027.
The SRR hike also soaks up the extra rupee liquidity created by the Central Bank's dollar purchases.
Despite May's 100bps hike, loan demand rose in 3Q26 (demand index 42.8 vs 35.1) while banks' willingness to lend fell (27.4 vs 40.4).
forecasts: Higher lending rates and slower credit growth ahead
Limited additional mark-to-market losses on banks' government securities portfolios, given the small size of the hike

news.title: Central Bank hikes policy rate to 9.00% and SRR to 3.00%
news.text: In a move markets did not expect, the Monetary Policy Board raised the OPR by 25bps to 9.00% and the SRR by 1 point to 3.00% (from the reserve period starting 9 Dec). Inflation reached 8.3% in October with core inflation also up; the Bank now expects inflation to stay above target for longer, returning to 5% in the second half of 2027. Reserves rose to about $7.1bn by end October through dollar purchases, which also flooded the money market with rupees. Separately, the Governor said total credit is still growing by more than 20% and the Bank has no credit target.

news.title: Hosking Partners buys 5.18% of JAT Holdings for Rs 1.05bn
news.text: Funds managed by UK-based Hosking Partners bought 27,077,498 JAT shares at Rs 38.8 each, the whole stake of the second-largest shareholder, Falcon Trading. Aelian Gunawardene keeps control with 63.63%. Hosking is also a top-20 holder in JKH, Aitken Spence, CT Holdings, Richard Pieris, Bukit Darah, Dialog, Tokyo Cement, Ceylon Guardian, Teejay and Lion Brewery; its Sri Lankan portfolio is reported to exceed $60mn.

news.title: Hosking: Sri Lanka must prove its recovery is lasting
news.text: Founder Jeremy Hosking called Budget 2027 encouraging and said the fund will stay invested (Sri Lanka is about 2% of its portfolio, across about 12 companies). It would commit much more only if the turnaround proves structural rather than cyclical, which resistance to change makes hard. He backed a currency board or even dollarisation and the removal of FX controls.

news.title: Budget 2027 needs more detail on trade and IMF: ODI
news.text: Think-tank ODI Global said the budget prioritises stability, productivity, exports, investment and digitalisation, but needs more specifics on trade integration, labour-market reform and future IMF work. It urged faster FTA negotiations, citing RCEP, a China FTA and deals with the UAE and Oman.

news.title: Analysts favour a follow-up IMF programme
news.text: The $2.9bn IMF programme ends in March 2027. Foreign debt repayments are nearly $3bn next year and $3.6bn in 2028. Fitch and Citi said a follow-on arrangement would anchor policy and support ratings; a committee is studying whether one is needed.

news.title: NSB Group 9M 2026: profit flat
news.text: National Savings Bank Group's net interest income rose 7.4% to Rs 69.1bn and pre-tax profit was Rs 34.7bn (Rs 34.8bn a year earlier); profit after tax was Rs 20.7bn. The bank had a Rs 4.1bn impairment reversal, offset partly by a Rs 744mn trading loss. Group equity rose 8.7% to Rs 139.05bn and assets to Rs 1.92tn.

news.title: Global: Anthropic's market debut; Japan inflation
news.text: Anthropic's Nasdaq debut valued it at about $1.76tn: shares priced at $83 rose as high as $111.53 and closed at $97.17, while the Nasdaq fell nearly 2.3%. Japan's October headline inflation rose to 2.3% as energy subsidies expired; core-core inflation eased to 2.2%.
